Works with

Rugged tablet for Salesforce Field Service

Salesforce Field Service is the field service management product of Salesforce, Inc., sold as an add-on to Service Cloud in the Enterprise, Unlimited and Developer editions. Dispatchers schedule service appointments in the dispatcher console inside Lightning Experience, and mobile workers receive and complete that work in the Field Service mobile app, published for Android and iOS. The Google Play listing (developer Salesforce.com, inc., updated 19 October 2026, more than 500,000 downloads, Phone and Tablet chips) describes an offline-first app with data priming, mapping and navigation, barcode and QR scanning, customer signatures, service reports and van stock. Each mobile user needs a Field Service Mobile user licence.

Unusually, Salesforce publishes a full device requirements table for the app, with recommended and minimum figures for operating system, memory, processor and storage, and a support schedule with an end-of-support date for each Android version. That makes the fit question answerable with dates rather than guesses, and the answer on 25 October 2026 is not the one a hardware seller would choose: none of the Tuga Android devices meets both the operating system floor and the memory floor at the same time, and Android 14 left support on 4 October 2026.

This page sets out what Salesforce publishes, says plainly which Tuga devices fall short and why, and explains where the Tuga W10 does fit: the dispatcher console and the rest of Lightning Experience in a supported desktop browser on a Windows tablet. It is written for service managers and the people who buy devices for them, who already run Salesforce Field Service or are deciding whether to. We do not describe any Tuga device as tested or certified with Salesforce software; the page matches Salesforce's published requirements to the published specifications of each device.

Requirements

What Salesforce Field Service (Field Service mobile app and dispatcher console) needs from a device

Each item below comes from Salesforce, Inc.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android operating system: latest major version minus two at minimum, the latest version recommended

    Salesforce's Technical Requirements for the Field Service Mobile App gives the minimum supported operating system as "Latest major Android version minus two (e.g., Android 15 if Android 17 is current)" and the recommended one as "Latest Android version provided by Google". Its support schedule lists end-of-support dates by version: Android 14 on 4 October 2026, Android 15 on 3 September 2027, Android 16 on 10 June 2028, and "Android 12 or earlier" on 4 October 2024. On 25 October 2026 the floor is therefore Android 15. Salesforce says it gives at least six months' notice before ending support for a version, and that once support ends new app releases are no longer tested on it and official fixes for issues specific to it stop. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Memory: 5GB RAM minimum with 2GB available to the app, 8GB or more recommended; 4GB or less is not supported

    The same table gives RAM as "8 GB+ (with 3 GB available to app)" recommended and "5 GB minimum (with 2 GB available to app)" as the minimum supported, with the note "Devices with 4 GB RAM or less are not supported and are prone to app crashes, memory issues, and degraded offline performance." The recommended figure is described as essential for priming 20,000 or more records for offline use, capturing high-resolution images or video, and running AI or augmented reality features. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Processor: Snapdragon 600 series or equivalent minimum, Snapdragon 700 series or better recommended

    Salesforce gives the CPU requirement as "Snapdragon 700 series or better (Android only)" recommended and "Snapdragon 600 series or equivalent" minimum. It does not publish an equivalence table for other processor families, and suggests benchmarking tools such as Geekbench or 3DMark to "check memory and CPU load under real-world conditions" before a rollout. The Tuga A10 and A8 use MediaTek processors and the A6 a MediaTek Helio P35; whether each is "equivalent" is Salesforce's judgement to make, not ours. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Storage: 5GB free minimum, 15GB free recommended

    Storage is given as "15 GB free" recommended and "5 GB free (insufficient for high volume briefcase implementations)" minimum. Every Tuga device except the A6 ships with 128GB; the A6 has 64GB plus a microSD slot. Free space after the operating system and other apps is what counts. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Device selection advice: rugged build, battery life, interchangeable batteries, mounts and a stylus

    The requirements article's Device Selection Guidance says to "Evaluate devices on real-world performance attributes like battery durability for long shifts, rapid charging or interchangeable batteries, thermal performance to prevent overheating and component degradation, and a rugged build quality that can handle tough environments", to consider "protective cases, secure mounts, and stylus input", to "Test Before You Buy" with a small batch under the team's real workload, and to plan a device refresh every three to four years. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Dispatcher console and Lightning Experience: latest stable Edge Chromium, Chrome, Firefox or Safari on a desktop or laptop; Android tablets only through the Salesforce mobile app

    Salesforce's Supported Browsers and Devices for Lightning Experience says desktop and laptop browsers must be the latest stable version of Microsoft Edge Chromium, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Apple Safari, that "Salesforce treats touch-enabled laptops, including Microsoft Surface and Surface Pro devices, as laptops instead of tablets", and for tablets that "We support only the Salesforce mobile app for Android-based tablets", with Chrome on Android marked not supported. Embedded WebView controls and private browsing modes are not supported. Source: help.salesforce.com

  • Licensing: the app needs a Field Service org and a Field Service Mobile user licence per user

    The Google Play listing says "This application requires your Salesforce org to have Field Service. Individual users must be provisioned with Field Service Technician licenses to use this application", and the requirements article says "To access the Field Service mobile app, users need the Field Service Mobile user license." Source: play.google.com

The Tuga W10 is the one device in the range with a straightforward fit, and it is for the office side of the product rather than the mobile app. It runs Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N100 with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it runs the latest stable Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome, which Salesforce supports for Lightning Experience and the dispatcher console, and Salesforce treats touch-enabled Windows devices as laptops rather than tablets. That makes it a rugged option for a supervisor or dispatcher who schedules from a van, a site cabin or a plant room, with a 10.1 inch screen, RJ45 Ethernet, HDMI and a removable 5000mAh battery. Worth knowing. The Tuga A10, A8 and A6 are not recommended for the Field Service mobile app on 25 October 2026. Salesforce's published minimum is the latest major Android version minus two, which is Android 15, with at least 5GB RAM and 4GB or less not supported, and its support schedule ended Android 14 support on 4 October 2026 and Android 12 support on 4 October 2024. The A10 (Android 14, 8GB RAM) fails on operating system, the A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM) fails on memory, and the A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM) fails on operating system. We publish no software update period for any model, so do not assume an update will change this. Salesforce also gives a processor floor of Snapdragon 600 series or equivalent without an equivalence table for MediaTek parts, which would need confirming even for a device that met the other figures. The Tuga W8 and WH6 are not in the recommended list because the mobile app is not published for Windows; like the W10 they could run Lightning Experience in a supported desktop browser, but the W10 is the one with the 10.1 inch screen and Ethernet that suits a dispatcher.
Setting up

Getting Salesforce Field Service (Field Service mobile app and dispatcher console) running

  1. Confirm with your Salesforce administrator that the org has Field Service enabled and that each mobile worker has a Field Service Mobile user licence; the app will not sign in without one.
  2. For dispatchers on a Tuga W10, install the latest stable Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome, sign in to Lightning Experience and open the Field Service app's dispatcher console; do not use private browsing, which Salesforce does not support.
  3. For mobile workers, choose a device that meets Salesforce's current minimum before you buy: Android 15 or later on 25 October 2026, at least 5GB RAM with 2GB free for the app, and 5GB free storage, with 8GB RAM and 15GB free recommended. Check the support schedule in the requirements article for the date your chosen Android version leaves support.
  4. Install the Field Service mobile app from Google Play (developer Salesforce.com, inc.) and sign in with the worker's Salesforce credentials; the administrator controls which records are primed for offline use and which Flows and quick actions appear.
  5. Follow Salesforce's advice to test a small batch of devices under the team's real workload, including a large offline priming and a full day in the field, before ordering a fleet, and benchmark memory and CPU with a tool such as Geekbench if the processor's equivalence is in doubt.
  6. Register each device's warranty at tugahardware.com/register-warranty and plan the refresh cycle Salesforce recommends, every three to four years, against the Android end-of-support dates it publishes.
